title.en: Circle games: Attakalam, Jodi Baki, Daicholu, Gocho Paari

text.en: In some games the circle is the field. A push, a number call, a crawl or a throw decides who stays in. Let us learn four circle games.

Attakalam: mark a big circle and form two teams of seven. One team stands inside, the other outside. Outside players go in and try to push inside players out, while the inside players resist. A student who pushes an opponent out within 30 seconds gets one point and the pushed student is out. If the student fails within 30 seconds, the opponent gets a point. The team with the most points or the most students left wins. It builds leg and arm strength and teamwork.
Jodi Baki: mark a circle with a radius of 7 metres. A leader stands inside and calls a number from 1 to 9. All the other students run slowly around the circle and, when a number is called, quickly form groups of that size by holding hands. Extra students who cannot join a full group are out. For 20 students and number 3, 6 groups are formed with 18 students and 2 are out.
The game continues with new numbers until only two or three students remain; they are the winners. If someone is left out, encourage them kindly - it is part of the game.
Daicholu: make a circular path and keep all students inside it. One is the chaser who crawls along the circle and touches others with the feet. A touched student is out. A student who steps outside the circle is disqualified. The first student touched becomes the next chaser. It develops core strength.
Gocho Paari: draw a smaller circle in the centre of a larger one. 7-8 students scatter in the bigger circle. A thrower tries to throw the ball into the inner circle while players try to stop it. If the ball gets in, the thrower enters the circle and the last player who tried to stop the ball becomes the thrower. Everyone gets a turn.
Variations: change the circle size, call numbers faster, use multiple balls, or play with legs only. Core muscles in the abdomen, back, hips and pelvis (about 29 in all) help us stand tall and balance.

problem.en: In Jodi Baki, 20 students are playing and the leader calls 3. How many are out?

text.en: Groups of 3 from 20: 20 / 3 = 6 groups with 2 left.
The 2 students left without a group are out.

prompt.en: Teach a friend the rules of Attakalam.

requiredIdeas.en: Two teams of seven, one inside and one outside the circle
Outside team pushes inside players out within 30 seconds
Points for successful pushes; most points or most students left wins

points.en: Attakalam: pushing within 30 seconds earns a point.
Jodi Baki: form groups of the called number; extras are out.
Daicholu: crawl and touch with the feet; stay inside the path.
Gocho Paari: stop the ball from entering the inner circle.
